findings.title: Subtransaction insertion bypasses committed-output barrier
findings.problem: xmin is the inserting subtransaction ID, whereas pg_current_xact_id() returns the top-level transaction ID. Their inequality does not prove that output committed. A receipt can therefore retain a pre-lock timestamp even when the entire output transaction commits after lock.
findings.reproduction: BEGIN; SAVEPOINT nested; INSERT vintage; RELEASE SAVEPOINT nested; INSERT receipt; hold outer transaction across lock; COMMIT. The receipt trigger accepts the still-uncommitted vintage.
findings.verification: Confirmed on isolated local PostgreSQL 17: inserting xmin 741, top transaction 740, top status in progress; receipt accepted; concurrent store.get returned null. No remote calls.
findings.repair: Store a server-assigned top-level xid8 for the output and require an explicit committed transaction status before issuing its receipt. Cover savepoints and delayed outer commit.

findings.title: History cursor silently loses receipts committed between pages
findings.problem: A fixed publication tuple upper bound is not a transaction snapshot. A receipt can acquire an early confirmed_at in an uncommitted transaction, then commit after the reader has advanced past its tuple. That immutable revision is absent from all subsequent pages of that traversal.
findings.reproduction: Commit vintage B, insert its receipt inside held transaction B. Publish C and D normally. Fetch page size 1 (C), commit B, fetch continuation (D). A fresh query sees B,C,D, but the paginated traversal sees only C,D.
findings.verification: Confirmed on isolated PostgreSQL 17: first=[review-3], rest=[review-4], freshRead=[review-2,review-3,review-4]. pg_visible_in_snapshot on B top xid against the initial snapshot returned false after B committed, validating the proposed snapshot fence primitive.
findings.repair: Pin an actual transaction-visibility snapshot in the cursor and filter all receipt rows by server-owned top-level receipt transaction identity, or provide another committed-order stable pagination guarantee. Cover delayed receipt commit, not only new publications started after page one.

findings.title: Observed play-begun state is lost when actual start is unknown
findings.problem: When a schedule observation says in_progress/suspended/final but actualStartAt is null, advanceLock closes only the returned boolean and leaves the prior epoch unchanged. Subsequent calls have no memory that play began and can reopen issuance.
findings.reproduction: Create initial lock; accept a suspended observation with actualStartAt=null; pass its returned epoch to a later scheduled observation with noPlayConfirmed=true and future start after the original lock. The final call reaches affirmative_no_play_reopening.
findings.verification: Source-traced; existing suspended-play test supplies an actual timestamp and does not cover the unknown-timestamp transition. No standalone execution performed.
findings.repair: Persist affirmative play-begun evidence independently of actualStartAt and never reopen a target after that evidence. Preserve timing uncertainty without erasing the lifecycle state.

findings.title: Participation replay can use bins fitted from future appearance labels
findings.problem: fitParticipation consumes calibration outcomes and returns bins without retaining their fitted/available-at clock. predictParticipation applies those bins to any context. Filtering raw training observations at the cutoff does not prevent leakage through the already fitted bins. CandidateModel similarly lacks a serving-time availability clock for its development-selected recipe.
findings.reproduction: Use model.test.ts fit fixture with fitAt Jan 30 and calibration rows 16/17. Apply fitted participation model to row 16 input cutoff Jan 17 instead of Jan 30. Its bin probability includes row 16 and row 17 appearance labels learned after that cutoff.
findings.verification: Source-traced; existing test predicts only at the final fit date, so it does not test pre-fit replay. No standalone execution performed.
findings.repair: Retain fitted/first-available and dependency chronology on models/calibrators; reject inference cutoffs before those dependencies were available. Keep development scoring helpers explicitly separated from admissible historical/public issuance.

findings.title: Frozen qualification scope requires hashes of future per-vintage predictions
findings.problem: qualificationScopeHash includes all manifest.artifactHashes, and frozen protocol/final/shadow/review records must match that digest and include those hashes (line 63). reproduceIntervals/verifyPin additionally requires each per-vintage JointDistribution hash in that manifest (uncertainty.ts:111). JointDistribution includes target and inputCutoffAt, so a newly issued future forecast necessarily requires a new hash. Preserving the original frozen evidence therefore makes ordinary future interval reproduction unavailable; updating it would rewrite preregistered evidence.
findings.reproduction: Take a valid pinnedScenario from uncertainty.test.ts. Produce a second vintage with a new input cutoff and correctly pinned corresponding joint payload, retaining the qualified model/calibration and frozen evidence. verifyPin rejects the new joint hash. Adding that hash to the manifest changes scopeHash and invalidates all frozen evidence.
findings.verification: Source-traced across qualification.ts:38,63 and uncertainty.ts:10-16,111,120-121. Current synthetic scenario precomputes future payload hashes into earlier evidence, hiding the temporal impossibility.
findings.repair: Separate frozen qualified model/calibration/decoder/algorithm applicability from dynamically generated per-vintage joint output pins. Bind each output to its qualified generator and immutable vintage without requiring its future bytes in the pre-evaluation protocol.
